Ranked ZIPs

Which rent applies

  • In HUD's 65 mandatory metros (Cleveland, Detroit, Philadelphia, Chicago, Atlanta, St. Louis, Memphis and others), each ZIP has its own payment standard. Cheap ZIPs get lower rents.
  • Everywhere else, housing authorities usually use one metro-wide rent, so a cheap ZIP gets the same rent as an expensive one. These rows carry an orange Metro tag.
  • Some housing authorities adopt ZIP rents voluntarily or set exception rents. Check the local schedule before you rely on a Metro-tagged rent. "Lower of the two" is the safe view.

Why the top ZIPs need a second look

  • Housing authorities test every lease for rent reasonableness. Where market rents run below the payment standard, the approved rent comes in lower.
  • The cheapest ZIPs usually need more rehab to pass inspection, and they carry more vacancy, turnover and crime risk. Raise the rehab and vacancy inputs to match.
  • Zillow values in small ZIPs are noisy. Leave "Skip the smallest ZIPs" on until you have a short list.

Before you trust a number

  • The payment standard covers rent plus tenant-paid utilities. If the tenant pays utilities, enter the local utility allowance.
  • Property tax and insurance vary a lot by state and city. Tax runs from under 1% of value to over 4% in some Midwest and Northeast cities. Insurance is far higher in Florida, Louisiana and Texas.
  • HUD's FY2027 rents take effect over the coming months and can move each ZIP up or down.

Sources: HUD User FY2026 Small Area FMRs · HUD FY2026 FMRs · HUD designated SAFMR areas · Zillow Research ZHVI by ZIP. Screening tool, not investment advice.
